title: Lacuna Ops - Security posture & hosting options evaluation
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary + cert links
Share draft network diagram for Private deployment within 3 business days
Schedule 1-hr dedicated SE benchmark run (throughput/latency) next week
action_items: Jordan Li - Email SOC2/ISO artifacts and security whitepaper - due 2027-08-27
Samir Patel - Prepare benchmark plan and cost estimate for Dedicated cluster - due 2027-08-30
Maya Chen - Share Lacuna's retention policy and list of required logs (Splunk) - due 2027-08-27
summary: Intro call focused on Lacuna's security and hosting requirements. Customer is considering Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key gaps: BYOK/KMS integration details, audit log forwarding and retention, SOC2 evidence, RBAC/SSO integration patterns, and network peering for Private. Agreed next steps: send certs, network diagram, and run benchmarks for Dedicated option.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-25 15:00 UTC, duration ~46m
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (Lacuna Security Lead), Alex Torres (Lacuna Platform), Renee Gomez (Lacuna Legal), Tom Beck (CTO)

00:00 Jordan Li: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood inference, i'm the ae for lacuna, um i'll hand it off to samir for a quick tech intro then we can dive into security and hosting options
00:14 Samir Patel: hi all, i'm samir, se on the account. quick agenda — confirm compliance reqs, sso/rbac patterns, encryption and kms questions, then deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and next steps
00:29 Maya Chen: thanks. our main driver is that we need to understand how we can meet SOC 2 type II evidence requirements and whether we can keep key material inside our KMS. Also retention — legal wants 7 years for certain logs but platform team prefers 1 year for app traces so, need to map that out
00:48 Tom Beck: and from infra perspective, we need predictable latency for customer-facing inference (sub 150ms p95) and isolation for PII workloads. we are open to hosted if isolation & kms are solved, otherwise we'll look at private deployment
01:08 Samir Patel: great. to be explicit — redwood hosted offers strong isolation tenant-wise but for BYOK we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and we also have a private deployment option where you can run the control plane inside your vpc and keys never leave your account
01:28 Maya Chen: can you clarify "support" for BYOK? are keys migrated to your HSM ephemeral or do we hold them? also auditability — our auditors will want proof that keys were never exported
01:40 Samir Patel: yes — so current model: for hosted we support a KMS integration where tokens are encrypted with your key (we use envelope encryption). the plaintext never leaves the hostbox. we can provide KMS audit log reference and attestation that keys are not exported. for dedicated and private, you can opt for kms-on-customer-side with the private control plane, and in that case redwood never has access to key material. (slight pause) Note: there are some implementation differences by cloud provider — we'll include provider-specific notes in the docs
02:12 Renee Gomez: legal would like to see encryption-at-rest certs and the exact SOC 2 report redacted; are you able to provide the Type II report and scope?
02:23 Jordan Li: absolutely, we can share the SOC 2 Type II report and we also maintain ISO 27001 cert. i'll attach the latest reports after this call
02:31 Maya Chen: about logs — we send all infra logs to splunk. can we forward your audit logs? and what's the retention window? we need immutable logs for 7 years for certain data access events
02:49 Samir Patel: audit logs are available via streaming — we support push to S3 and direct integration with common SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, etc). retention is configurable; hosted default is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on. for compliance, we can escrow logs to your s3 bucket with object lock for immutability if required
03:16 Alex Torres: good. any PII redaction or archival workflows we should know about? we have regulated data, so both encryption and record lifecycle matter
03:29 Samir Patel: we have redaction options at ingestion and can also configure prompt-level token scrubbing, though that impacts latency in some edge cases. lifecycle rules are configurable for both KV cache and request logs
03:45 Priya Rao: to speak to RBAC — by default we offer role-based roles scoped to teams, organization admins, and read-only viewers. for enterprise, we integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. you can map SCIM groups to RBAC roles
04:04 Maya Chen: will group sync be one-way from our IDP? we want control over who gets admin privileges, not redwood changing groups
04:13 Priya Rao: yes group sync is one-way from your idp to redwood. provisioning/ deprovisioning is via SCIM and you retain control. we log changes to role mappings for audit
04:29 Renee Gomez: any SOC 2 controls around access reviews? auditors ask for periodic access review evidence
04:36 Jordan Li: we can export access review logs and attest to quarterly review workflows; we can also integrate with your GRC tools if you use them
04:47 Tom Beck: network-wise — for private deployment, what's the model for peering? we need to avoid public ingress for inference traffic
04:56 Samir Patel: private is either vpc peering or a private subnet approach with customer-managed NAT. control plane can be in your VPC or run on-prem. we support TLS mutual auth between control plane and workers plus strict security groups. hosted goes over TLS and supports IP allowlists and customer-managed VPC outbound endpoints for egress control
05:24 Maya Chen: are there specific attestation docs for mTLS? our infosec wants to include those in the security pack
05:31 Samir Patel: yes we'll provide mTLS handshake diagrams and cert rotation policies — and a design doc for key rotation cadence
05:43 Alex Torres: about audit trails — we need proof of model versioning and who invoked what model and what prompt template was used. does redwood keep that lineage by default?
05:55 Samir Patel: yes we maintain request lineage: model id, runtime image, prompt meta, tokens, and a request id. by default request payloads are logged but you can toggle redaction. we store metadata for lineage even if you choose to redact content
06:12 Maya Chen: okay but retention for lineage vs content are different. we need metadata retained for 7 years but content only 90 days. can you do differential retention?
06:25 Samir Patel: yes, differential retention is supported — we'll put raw content in shorter retention buckets and metadata in longer ones. we also support event export to your S3 for long-term retention with lifecycle rules you control
06:40 Renee Gomez: does redwood support CJIS-like requirements or is that out of scope? (unclear pronunciation)
06:48 Jordan Li: we don't have CJIS certs out of the box; we can discuss controls that map to CJIS if required but private deployment on-prem is the usual path for that level of control
07:00 Tom Beck: what about pen testing and vulnerability scan reports? our security team wants to see recent pentest results and remediation timelines
07:10 Samir Patel: yes we have quarterly vulnerability scans and annual pentests; we can share redacted reports and a summary of critical findings and remediation timelines
07:21 Maya Chen: SCIM - provisioning - can you confirm the SCIM attributes supported? we rely heavily on custom attributes for role mapping
07:29 Priya Rao: we support the common SCIM schema plus custom attributes via extension; we'll include a sample SCIM payload in the doc set
07:39 Alex Torres: for Private deployment how much ops overhead is expected on our side? we want a sense of runbook and what Redwood still manages
07:49 Samir Patel: for private, we provide a managed operator and deployment scripts; your team handles the VPC, subnet, and KMS, while redwood runs the control plane operator and provides upgrades, monitoring hooks, and support. we also offer a dedicated SLA-backed package where we do more of the heavy lifting
08:12 Maya Chen: latency and throughput — can you give rough numbers for dedicated cluster with A100-style GPUs? our p95 target is 150ms for the 512-token average workload
08:26 Samir Patel: ballpark — with optimized kernels and batching you can hit 100-130ms p95 for 512 tokens on a properly sized dedicated pool; we'll validate with a benchmark run. hosted latencies vary a bit more due to multi-tenant scheduling
08:39 Tom Beck: cost is obviously a factor — we need a cost/latency tradeoff for dedicated vs hosted. also whats the minimum commitment for a Dedicated pool
08:50 Jordan Li: dedicated minimum is typically a monthly reserved pool, numbers vary by region and instance type — we'll include a detailed cost model in the follow-up along with the benchmark results
09:03 Maya Chen: about data deletion — can we request full purge of content on demand across all storage backends? our privacy policy requires timely deletion for subject requests
09:15 Samir Patel: yes we offer purge APIs and workflows; on hosted, purge completes within the SLA window, and for private, you have local control. note that some derived artifacts (aggregated metrics) are kept in anonymized form by default but we can configure stricter deletion
09:34 Renee Gomez: do you support contractual language for data residency and deletion SLAs? we need that in the MSA
09:41 Jordan Li: yes we can add contractual clauses for residency and deletion timeframes; redwood legal is used to enterprise redlines and we'll work them with you
09:50 Alex Torres: are there any hard blockers for forwarding audit logs to our splunk? e.g., format or PII handling concerns
10:00 Samir Patel: no major blockers — logs can be forwarded in JSON with configurable fields. we can filter PII fields before forwarding if you want. for immutability use S3 object lock with us providing the export stream
10:18 Maya Chen: for SSO we use Okta and want SAML with enforced MFA for admins. does redwood support enforcing MFA through IdP assertions?
10:29 Priya Rao: we rely on IdP to assert auth context. we honor the MFA enforcement from your IdP and we gate admin actions with additional approval flows if desired
10:40 Tom Beck: on RBAC, can we have separation between model ops and infra ops? different levels of access?
10:48 Priya Rao: yes we support fine-grained roles; model ops can be limited to model deployment and monitoring while infra ops control keys and network
10:57 Maya Chen: can we get an example of the audit log schema? we need it to map to our SIEM ingestion pipeline
11:05 Samir Patel: we'll attach an example logfile; expect fields like timestamp, actor, action, resource_id, model_version, request_id, and a diff of role changes
11:16 Maya Chen: what about tamper-evidence for logs? our auditors ask for chain-of-custody ideas
11:23 Samir Patel: recommended approach is push to your S3 with object lock + periodic signed manifests; we can also provide signed log hashes on request for the period of the engagement
11:38 Alex Torres: how is kernel selection / optimizations handled in dedicated? any chance my team needs to manage that?
11:47 Samir Patel: that's handled by the runtime — redwood picks kernels per model and sequence profile; for private we give tuning knobs but our SEs can run the tuning during onboarding
12:00 Jordan Li: quick pivot — competitors. are you evaluating other vendors?
12:05 Maya Chen: yes, we are speaking with Anthropic and also looking at managed vertex endpoints and an internal POC. Anthropic is interesting for compliance packages but not sure about cost
12:15 Jordan Li: useful to know; we'll highlight where redwood differentiates on ops controls and predictable pricing
12:22 Renee Gomez: legal question: if we run private on our cloud, what is the liability boundary for data breaches? need to see a recommended language
12:32 Jordan Li: we can provide suggested MSA language and will flag typical carve-outs for customer-managed infrastructure. we'll loop legal teams together in the next exchange
12:40 Maya Chen: any limitations on model catalog for private? we need access to some custom models and quantized variants
12:48 Samir Patel: private and dedicated both support bringing your own model artifacts; runtime supports quantized weights and custom kernels though some unsupported ops may require a compatibility shim
12:58 Alex Torres: for the benchmark — can you run our 1k-request replay to mimic production traffic? we can provide a dataset (anonymized)
13:06 Samir Patel: yes we do replay-based benchmarks; please provide dataset and expected traffic profile, we'll run it in a dedicated sandbox and produce a latency/cost report
13:16 Maya Chen: and lastly, incident response — who owns notifications and SLAs?
13:23 Jordan Li: redwood owns platform incidents; for private the initial detection is ours if managed, but notification and escalation matrix is defined in the SLA. we'll share our incident response playbook
13:36 Priya Rao: summary of deliverables: SOC2/ISO certs, SCIM payload example, audit log schema, private deployment network diagram template, benchmark plan and cost estimate
13:48 Maya Chen: sounds good. thanks. we'll review materials and regroup after the benchmark results

End transcript (note: transcription contains occasional mishears; e.g., "hostbox" maybe "host box"; "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache").
